chainSteps.label: Mechanism & pharmacology
chainSteps.reasoning: Mechanism signal strength: moderate (MSS 0.47). Potency profile (IPS 0.51): potency 0.40, selectivity 0.62, PK 0.50, engagement 0.38, therapeutic window 0.72. Translational reliability (TRS 0.47): target validation 0.35, indication fit 0.72, modality fit 0.58, translation rate 0.12. Uncertainty (σ² 0.35).

chainSteps.label: Animal model: multi-tumor xenograft/orthotopic efficacy (TNBC, PDAC, GBM) — no CRC-specific model
chainSteps.reasoning: TTX-MC138 has a substantial preclinical in vivo package across multiple murine tumor models, though none is CRC-specific. In TNBC models, treatment eliminated pre-existing local metastases in 100% of treated animals (stage II/III) and distant metastases in 65% (stage IV). In an orthotopic PDAC xenograft, 40% of animals achieved complete responses (regression without recurrence), with necropsy confirming no residual tumors or metastases and gene expression confirming target engagement. In orthotopic GBM murine models, IV-delivered TTX-MC138 produced a five-fold increase in tumor apoptosis and a statistically significant survival extension, published peer-reviewed in the Journal of Functional Biomaterials (Jan 2026). IND-enabling PK, biodistribution, and toxicity studies are complete, with a rat NOAEL of 1 mg/kg (IV). These are genuinely strong preclinical signals — mu is set above average (~1.2) reflecting consistent, multi-model efficacy with solid mechanistic readouts. However, sigma2 is kept moderately wide (0.38) for two reasons: (1) no CRC-specific model exists, making the indication-match indirect; and (2) the target indication is MRD (micrometastatic/ctDNA-positive), a setting with no direct animal analog — the murine models used established macro-metastatic disease, which is a different biological and clinical context from eradicating minimal residual disease post-curative-intent surgery.

chainSteps.label: Same-target: MN-anti-miR10b (TTX-MC138 precursor, Phase 0/1a); Modality-class: MRX34 (miR-34a mimic, Phase 1 terminated), Cobomarsen/MRG-106 (anti-miR-155, Phase 2 discontinued) — miRNA-directed oncology class track record
chainSteps.reasoning: TIER 1 (same target): TTX-MC138 itself is the only anti-miR-10b agent to enter human trials; it completed Phase 1a with no dose-limiting toxicities and 64% stable disease in 14 evaluable patients, but zero confirmed objective responses — stable disease only in a heavily pre-treated metastatic population is a weak efficacy signal. TIER 2 (same modality-class — miRNA-directed oncology therapeutics): MRX34 (liposomal miR-34a mimic) was terminated in Phase 1 after four patient deaths from immune-mediated adverse events, with only 3 partial responses in 85 patients; Cobomarsen (anti-miR-155 LNA antagomir) was discontinued after Phase 2 without achieving its endpoints in lymphoma — collectively this constitutes at least two well-documented clinical failures across different companies and miRNA targets with no approved or pivotal-success analog in this modality class. TIER 3 (broader RNA/oligonucleotide oncology): the broader therapeutic-oligonucleotide oncology space has likewise produced no approved cancer drugs via this route. The miRNA-directed oncology modality is a class graveyard: no approved agents, multiple Phase 1–2 failures, and safety signals (immune-mediated toxicity) that challenge the delivery platform broadly. TTX-MC138's own Phase 1a 'stable disease only' signal in metastatic disease — while its Phase 2a targets the easier MRD/ctDNA+ setting — partially offsets the class-level negativity, and its clean safety profile differentiates it from MRX34; however, efficacy translation from stable disease in late-line metastatic to ctDNA clearance in MRD remains unproven. Synthesis: the class graveyard with 2–3 documented failures justifies a low mu (0.30) reflecting the strong negative class prior, with sigma2 set at 0.18 — lower than a single-failure scenario but slightly elevated above the tightest range because TTX-MC138's own tolerability data and distinct delivery chemistry introduce modest uncertainty about whether it will track the class trajectory.

chainSteps.label: Own clinical data: Phase 1a dose-escalation (n=14–16 evaluable, metastatic mixed solid tumors, RECIST tumor response)
chainSteps.reasoning: The completed Phase 1a trial (NCT06260774) enrolled 16 patients with advanced metastatic solid tumors across 4 dose cohorts; 14 were evaluable for RECIST tumor response. The headline efficacy result was 64% stable disease lasting ≥6 months — zero objective responses (PR/CR) were reported. Stable disease only in a RECIST-measured setting is null_negative under the scoring rules: no objective responses were achieved, which is the clinically meaningful efficacy bar. This anchors mu at 0.38 (well below average; clearly weak efficacy signal, not near-failure-zero but stable disease carries some minor informational weight). Two major translation gaps compound the scoring: (1) the Phase 1a evidence comes from a mixed metastatic solid-tumor population, whereas the valued indication is ctDNA-positive/MRD CRC post-curative-intent surgery — a completely different biology (no measurable disease, ctDNA clearance endpoint, not RECIST), adding ~+0.25–0.30 to sigma2; (2) the small n (14 evaluable) and mixed histology further widen uncertainty. Despite the mismatch, the ASYMMETRY rule prevents sigma2 from being inflated to the point of neutralizing the null signal — sigma2 is set at 0.48, reflecting modest confidence in the negative (small n limits certainty but the 0-ORR result is still informative-negative), with a moderate upward adjustment for the cross-setting/endpoint translation gap.

stages.name: TTX-MC138 Phase 2a — ctDNA Clearance & RFS in MRD-Positive CRC
stages.phase: Phase 2a (INITIATED) — ctDNA+ colorectal MRD. The ClinicalTrials.gov label for the master IND is Phase 1/2 (NCT06260774); the Phase 1a dose-escalation arm (the safety gate) is COMPLETE as of June 2026. The active efficacy-bearing arm is Phase 2a (NCT05868226), initiated May 2026.
stages.aiRationale: Phase 2a single-arm proof-of-concept with RFS as primary gate; ctDNA clearance rate as co-primary biomarker proof-of-concept. If RFS signal is strong (>70% at interim/primary), this supports pivotal Phase 3 initiation.

trialDesign.endpointDescription: ctDNA clearance rate (circulating tumor DNA negativity) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) in ctDNA-positive stage II-IV colorectal cancer patients post-curative therapy
trialDesign.enrollmentNote: Phase 2a single-arm open-label trial in ctDNA-positive colorectal MRD (minimal residual disease); initiated May 2026 following Phase 1a dose-escalation safety gate completion (June 2026). Biomarker-selected population (ctDNA+). Typical Phase 2a enrollment ~60 patients; no BTD or orphan designation confirmed for this indication.

stages.endpointRationale: RFS is the primary gating endpoint because in the MRD setting, ctDNA clearance alone (a biomarker surrogate) cannot support approval without clinical benefit data; RFS is the time-to-event measure that bridges biomarker signal to clinical outcome and is the FDA-accepted pivotal endpoint in adjuvant/MRD CRC (KEYNOTE-177, MCODE trial precedent).
stages.comparatorSource: Historical RFS in observation-only or standard adjuvant therapy in ctDNA-positive MRD CRC: ~40–50% 2-year RFS from MCODE (Gensheimer et al., ASCO GI 2024) and supportive real-world data; nullResponseRate set to 15% for untreated ctDNA-positive MRD baseline hazard.

stages.name: TTX-MC138 Phase 3 Registration — RFS in MRD-Positive CRC vs Observation
stages.aiRationale: Phase 3 randomized trial (TTX-MC138 vs observation, 1:1 or similar) to confirm RFS benefit and generate the registration package. FDA will expect ~18–24 month median follow-up to mature RFS events; interim futility/efficacy analysis planned at 50% events.

trialDesign.endpointDescription: Disease-free survival (DFS) — time to recurrence or death
trialDesign.enrollmentNote: n=280 (1:1 randomized), multi-center RCT at 40–60 specialized oncology sites; enrollment ~6 patients/month over ~47 months; observation arm is standard of care comparator

stages.endpointRationale: DFS/RFS is the FDA-registrable primary endpoint for adjuvant/MRD colorectal cancer (ALTAIR, DYNAMIC-III, CLAUDIA); ctDNA clearance is a supportive secondary, not the registrational basis. Pinned to regulatory precedent.
stages.comparatorSource: Observation (standard of care) arm measured concurrently in Phase 3 RCT; historical baseline 2-year RFS ~50% in untreated ctDNA-positive MRD CRC from MCODE and supportive registries.
